answer: An agent market assigns voting weight to escrowed tokens, with each token counted once, regardless of account count. Whether agents rent a wharf, survey a knoll, or sell a quill, voting requires locking tokens for 30 days. Splitting 1,000 tokens among a thousand fake identities still buys only 1,000 tokens of weight. More influence requires more locked capital, costing the attacker liquidity and returns available elsewhere.
